title: 2026-10-22_Sandworm_Incident_Response_Exercise_271
description: Investigate and respond to a Sandworm intrusion using the P.A.S. webshell backdoor on a compromised Centreon system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Centreon system at your organization has been compromised by the Sandworm intrusion set, specifically using the P.A.S. webshell backdoor. This malware provides capabilities for file manipulation, network tools, SQL client connections, and password brute-forcing. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is at IP address `192.168.50.5`. Enter `start` to begin the exercise.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the target system for unauthorized or suspicious services running on the host. What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target system?
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The suspicious service is likely related to the P.A.S. webshell backdoor. The final flag is `payload-transfer.service`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. What is the name of the timer used for persistence by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Examine the systemd unit files and timers to identify how the service is set to start automatically. The persistence mechanism is likely related to the P.A.S. webshell backdoor. The final flag is `payload-transfer.timer`.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for suspicious activity on the host. What is the full path of the process responsible for the suspicious activity?
levels.solution: Use process monitoring tools to identify any unusual processes and correlate them with the suspicious service. The process is likely related to the P.A.S. webshell backdoor. The final flag is `/usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh`.
